'''Robert John Audley''' was a British psychologist whose research was concerned with choice and decision-making.

==Career==
'''Robert (Bob) Audley''' was born in London in 1925. Following [[national service]], he obtained his BSc from [[University College London]] in 1949.  Among his lecturers was [[E.S. Pearson]]. He then obtained a [[Fulbright scholarship]] which took him to [[Washington State University]]. On his return he completed a PhD supervised by [[Aimable Robert Jonckheere|A.R. Jonckheere]] at [[University College London|UCL]].<ref>{{cite thesis |type=Ph.D. |last=Audley|first=Robert J. |date=1956 |title=Stochastic processes and the description of learning behaviour in choice situations |publisher=University of London}}</ref> He was appointed to the faculty and remained there for the whole of his academic career.  He served as head of department.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Harvey |first1=Nigel |title=Robert (Bob) Audley 1928-2020 |journal=The Psychologist |date=2020}}</ref>

He was active in the British Psychological Society of which he became president in 1981. His Presidential address was on the subject of choice.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Audley |first1=Robert |title=Choosing |journal=Bulletin of the British Psychological Society |date=1970 |volume=23 |pages=177–191}}</ref> He was Editor of the [[British Journal of Mathematical and Statistical Psychology]] from 1963 to 1969. He was also President of the Experimental Psychology Society about which he was interviewed.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bob Audley Interview |url=https://soundcloud.com/user-299561354/bob-audley-interview-for-the-eps |website=Cubistular |access-date=26 August 2020}}</ref>

==Research==
There were three strands to his research. The first strand, as a mathematical psychologist, he developed a Theory of Choice to explain the process of decision-making (Audley, 1960; Audley & Pike, 1965). His second strand was on reaction time (Audley, Caudrey, Howell and Powell, 1975) and the third was on medical accidents (Audley, Vincents & Ennis, 1993).
